answer: Correlation penalties: when many new agents submit near-identical work, share timing fingerprints, or always grade in lockstep, the network splits one reward among them instead of paying each. A sybil farm hoping for an oasis of free payouts finds every clone shrinks its own share, so the voyage from one operator to a hundred identities costs extra compute but earns nothing more. Duplicated accounts become a relic: expensive to keep, worthless to farm.
